headline: Referred automated traffic enforcement ordinance back to committee to remove speed camera references, 4-2; approved $34,805 carryover request.
summary: The board heard public comment on automated traffic enforcement devices and on crosswalk signals. A 4-2 vote referred the traffic enforcement ordinance back to the Ordinance Committee to remove references to speed cameras. The board also approved a $34,805 carryover request from the Board of Finance.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 21, 2026 meeting, unanimously.
Approved monthly reports and placed them on file, unanimously.
Placed on file the response from Corporation Counsel about the ordinance authorizing automated traffic enforcement safety devices, unanimously.
Placed on file the disposition report on the complaint against the Chief and Deputy Chief, unanimously. The outcome was no cause found for discipline.
Referred the automated traffic enforcement ordinance back to the Ordinance Committee to remove references to speed cameras, 4-2.
Approved the carryover of $34,805 requested by the Board of Finance, unanimously.

plain_text:
BOARD OF POLICE COMMISSIONERS 
REGULAR MEETING 
                                                      AUGUST 18, 2026, AT 6:00 p.m. 
COUNCIL CHAMBERS 
 
PRESENT:             ABSENT:  
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Chairperson    Commissioner Gloria Sapp Smith   
Commissioner Rory Ghio - via Zoom 
Commissioner Dean Kilbourne         
Commissioner Paul Lemieux 
Commissioner Terry Lewis 
Council Member Sue Tyler               
Board of Finance Liaison, Jon Mace 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
2. AWARDS 
Officers McNally, Genovese, and Gotowala received the Life Saving Award regarding an incident on 
June 21, 2026.  Officer McNally was also awarded Officer of the Month for July, 2026. 
 
Detective Verillo, Officers Genovese, Bazarewsky, Giannini, and Southington Detective Thomson were 
awarded the Silver Star Award. 
 
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
Gabby Carrano, 70 Seneca Road, spoke in opposition to license plate readers, red light cameras, and 
speed cameras. 
 
Mary Ann Sirois, 362 Shrub Road, spoke in opposition to the use of automated traffic enforcement 
safety devices. 
 
Duane Mack, 67 Stearns Street, spoke regarding the need for crosswalk signals through the City. 
 
Shelley Mastroianni, 120 Sixth Street, spoke in opposition to the use of automated traffic enforcement 
safety devices.  
 
4. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
Council Member Tyler moved to APPROVE THE MINUTES FROM THE JULY 21, 2026, REGULAR 
POLICE BOARD, seconded by Commissioner Lemieux. 
 
VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED  
 
5. APPROVAL OF VARIOUS MONTHLY REPORTS 
Commissioner Kilbourne moved to APPROVE MONTHLY REPORTS AND PLACE ON FILE, 
seconded by Commissioner Ghio. 
 
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED
6. CORRESPONDENCE 
None 
 
7. COMMITTEE MINUTES 
None 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
a. Chief Morello 
i. LPR Transparency Portal 
Chief Morello reviewed the Flock transparency portal, which is located on the City of Bristol Police 
Department’s website under Useful Resources: Bristol CT PD Transparency Portal. 
 
b. Police Commissioners 
i. Response from Corporation Counsel regarding the ordinance authorizing the use of automated traffic 
enforcement safety devices. 
Commissioner Kilbourne made a motion TO PLACE ON FILE THE RESPONSE FROM 
CORPORATION COUNSEL REGARDING THE ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE USE OF 
AUTOMATED TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT SAFETY DEVICES, seconded by Commissioner Lewis. 
 
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
ii. Report as to the disposition of complaint filed against the Chief and Deputy Chief. 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu responded that the summaries have been distributed to the Police Commission.  The 
outcome was no cause found for discipline or any action to be taken against the Chief or Deputy Chief.  
Some recommendations were made regarding processes and procedures, and most of those changes have 
already been implemented. 
 
Commissioner Kilbourne made a motion TO PLACE ON FILE, seconded by Commissioner Lewis. 
 
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
Council member Tyler discussed the ordinance authorizing the use of automated traffic enforcement 
safety devices.  
Council member Tyler made a motion to REFER BACK TO THE ORDINANCE COMMITTEE TO 
REMOVE ANY REFERENCE TO SPEED CAMERAS, INCLUDING DEFINITIONS THAT 
INCLUDE SPEED CAMERAS, seconded by Commissioner Lemieux.  
 
A discussion was held regarding the motion.  Mayor Zoppo Sassu called for a roll call vote on whether 
to refer this back to the Ordinance Committee. 
 
Commissioner Kilbourne - no 
Commissioner Lemieux - yes 
Council Member Tyler - yes 
Commissioner Lewis - yes 
Commissioner Ghio - yes 
Chairperson Mayor Zoppo Sassu – no 
 
     
             VOTE: PASSED   YES – 4  NO – 2
9.  NEW BUSINESS 
a. Chief Morello 
i. Chief’s Report 
Chief Morello reviewed the monthly Chief’s report. 
 
ii. Board of Finance Request 
Commissioner Ghio moved to APPROVE THE CARRYOVER OF $34,805, Seconded by 
Commissioner Kilbourne. 
 
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED 
 
b. Police Commissioners 
i. Bristol Vision Zero Initiative 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu discussed the Bristol Vision Zero Initiative with the Board. 
 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu asked if there were any other questions or concerns. Chief Morello responded with 
a question to Council Member Tyler about a post she made on Facebook. Council Member Tyler 
responded that it was a sarcastic response to a sarcastic comment. 
 
 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
Commissioner Lemieux moved to ADJOURN, Seconded by Council Member Tyler. 
  
             VOTE: UNANIMOUSLY PASSED  
 
 
The regular meeting of the Board of Police Commissioners called for the 18th day of August, 2026, was 
HEREBY ADJOURNED AT 6:54 p.m. 
 
 
 
                   Lisa Ziogas                   Recording Secretary
